neutral_facts.value: The incident occurred at approximately 12:45 a.m. on April 21, 2011, in the area of Baba Rasoi Dhaba, Jalandhar. The deceased was involved in a dispute with the accused, who were his friends. The deceased was found grappling with the accused on a street. The deceased approached the accused, and after a confrontation, A1 took out a gun and shot the deceased. The accused were present at the scene, and there was a fight. The deceased was taken to a hospital, and the accused were later charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The trial court convicted all accused under Section 304 part I IPC with life sentences, but the High Court and Supreme Court found the evidence insufficient to establish common intention for A3 and A4, leading to their acquittal.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused A3 and A4 instigated A1 to shoot the deceased, and that the common intention under Section 34 IPC was established. They relied on the statement of PW6, who initially did not mention the instigation but later improved his statement to include it.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the courts should have disbelieved the evidence of PW6, as it was an improvement to his earlier statement. They contended that there was no sufficient evidence to prove that A3 and A4 were aware that A1 had a gun, and that the prosecution failed to meet the burden of proof under Section 34 IPC.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that Section 34 IPC creates a deeming fiction by attributing an offence committed by one to others acting in furtherance of a common intention. The prosecution must prove the common intention to the satisfaction of the court with substantial, concrete, and clear evidence.
